bib.title: Design Docs Are All You Need: An AI-native Machine-Learning Performance Tool

legacy_report:
COVERAGE: 5 of 5 pages, 16,075 of 16,075 chars (extraction was clean). No appendices exist; the paper is a short 5-page preprint. Figure captions were not run through the figures script. Figure 1 is visible in the text extraction.

SOURCE: "Design Docs Are All You Need: An AI-native Machine-Learning Performance Tool" (the library is called SMART). Authors: Samuel Kushnir, Kimia Noorbakhsh, Kavya Sreedhar, Liqun Cheng, Ming Liu, Parthasarathy Ranganathan, Mohammad Alizadeh, Fred Kjolstad, Suvinay Subramanian. Affiliations: Google DeepMind, MIT, Stanford, Google. Venue: arXiv preprint 2609.05364v1 [cs.PL], 4 Sep 2026. The task called it "AI-Native Design Docs"; the PDF title is the one above.

CORE CLAIM: SMART's main branch holds almost no code. It holds a DAG of self-contained natural-language design docs (markdown). Coding sub-agents regenerate the implementation from the docs alone on each version update, and humans edit only the docs. The docs are the durable artifact and code is a build product. Regeneration drives "incremental generation debt" to zero by construction.

CLAIMS AND NUMBERS (all setup details are what the paper states; there is no results table)
1. SMART comprises 50 design docs, about 9,000 lines of spec prose. Setup: the Google ML performance-modeling library for TPUs.
   Quote: "SMART today comprises 50 design docs ( ∼9,000 lines of specification prose)" (p.4)
2. Full clean-slate regeneration takes 1.5 to 3 hours and costs about 100 USD, roughly 20% of a weekly Claude Max budget. Setup: Claude Code; the model is not named, and n and the number of runs are not given.
   Quote: "a full clean-slate regeneration of the library takes between 1.5 and 3 hours. The API cost for a complete rebuild using Claude Code is around 100 USD" (p.3)
3. Regenerated implementations reproduce hand-audited reference models "to round-off precision", including DeepSeek-V3 serving on a TPU pod slice. This is stated only in the abstract. There is no table, no count of models, and no pass rate. (p.1)
4. Three benefits of one sub-agent per doc: bounded context, targeted human iteration via the orchestrator's log of where agents struggled, and dynamic model routing. Routing means larger models for foundational docs and cheaper ones downstream. No ablation supports any of the three. (p.2-3)

DESIGN POINTS RELEVANT TO NOTE 09
- Dependency edges are machine-discovered by read-only agents, not hand-maintained. An orchestrator walks the DAG in topological order and keeps a log of prose the sub-agents misread. (p.2)
- Worked examples, a bottom-up complement to rules/tests (a "constitution"): step-by-step traces of intermediate values act as in-context demonstrations. (p.3)
- Every number-bearing doc ends with a "reconciliation anchor", a small preset with exactly stated expected outputs that generated tests enforce. (p.3)
- A claimed side effect is that vague intent surfaces early, because a guess must be written into a doc to survive. (p.4)

QUOTES
- "Our main branch contains almost no code. Instead, it consists of a folder structure of design document markdown files that compose into a directed acyclic graph (DAG)." (p.2)
- "a concrete trace pins down semantics that prose alone leaves ambiguous" (p.3)
- "every number-bearing doc ends with a reconciliation anchor: a small preset whose expected outputs are stated exactly and enforced by generated tests." (p.3)
- "surfaces vague intent early, because a guess must be written into a doc to survive." (p.4)

LIMITS
- This is a position/system-description paper with no experiments. It has no baseline of incremental or human-patched development, no ablation of worked examples versus none, and no measurement of debt D_t, bug rates, or doc-edit effort.
- There is no number of regeneration runs, no variance, no failure rate, and no model name or version. Cost and time are single self-reported figures.
- Correctness evidence is only the abstract's "round-off" claim against hand-built references. It is not tabulated, so it is unverifiable from the paper.
- The result may not carry over from this domain. The domain is narrow, symbolic and numerically checkable, which suits regeneration because outputs can be reconciled exactly. The paper itself says only that the approach "should generalize wherever specs churn faster than software absorbs them."
- Equation 1's claim that debt goes to zero is true by definition of full regeneration. It says nothing about regeneration quality.
- The "context-window myopia" argument is asserted, not measured.
- A handful of leaf utilities remain as code. Tests and reconciliation references are hand-built, so humans still own verification.

BUILDS ON
- In-context learning: Brown et al., 2020 (NeurIPS) and the Dong et al., 2022 survey (arXiv). These credit the worked-example idea.
- Roofline: Williams et al., 2009 (CACM).
- Iterative modulo scheduling: Rau, 1994 (MICRO).
- SymPy: Meurer et al., 2017.
- TPU v4: Jouppi et al., 2023 (ISCA).
- It does not cite prior AGENTS.md or repo-as-record work, or any spec-driven-development literature.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Figure 1, p.2, "The regeneration workflow: sub-agents regenerate the implementation from the design-doc DAG in dependency order, and the result must pass reconciliation against hand-built references before it replaces the previous build. Humans only ever edit the docs."

HONEST FIT: This is a weak source with only partial fit. It is a short, unreviewed preprint with essentially no empirical evidence. About 60% of it (Section 3, the symbolic Op IR and its DSL) is irrelevant to harness engineering. It is useful only as an illustrative extreme case of "the repo is the system of record": docs as source, code as build output, worked examples plus exact reconciliation anchors, and an orchestrator log that tells humans which docs are unclear. It should be cited as a design position or example, not as evidence that the approach works. It says nothing on AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md entry files.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The extraction has minor spacing faults ("Y ou", "describeSMART"). The arXiv ID 2609.05364 and the Sep 2026 date are as printed in the PDF. The file is at /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/03-harness-engineering/sources/kushnir-2026-design-docs-all-you-need.pdf.
